chunks: Indeed, when the stranger is approached by death, he turns to the right and to the left and sees no one. He raises his head, and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: “To whom are you turning? To one who is better for you than Me? By My might and My majesty, if I release you from your bond, I shall surely place you in My obedience, and if I seize you, I shall surely place you into My honor.”

key_terms.الْغَرِيبَ: the stranger, one away from his people and support
key_terms.الْمَوْتُ: death, the moment of departing this world
key_terms.طَاعَتِي: My obedience, a life directed toward obeying Allah
key_terms.كَرَامَتِي: My honor, divine dignity and gracious treatment
key_terms.وَعِزَّتِي وَجَلَالِي: an oath by divine might and majesty

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith teach about the stranger at the time of death and Allah’s care for him?
ai.summary: This hadith depicts the loneliness of the stranger at the moment of death and directs attention to Allah as the only true refuge and caretaker. It emphasizes Allah’s might, majesty, and generosity, showing that whether life continues or death comes, the believer remains under divine care and honor.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: "When a stranger faces death, he looks to his right and left but sees no one. He raises his head, and Allah (swt), the Mighty and Glorious, says: 'To whom do you turn? To one who is better for you than Me? By My might and My majesty, if I release you from this bond, I will place you in My obedience, and if I take your soul, I will place you in My honor.'"
